deep.reconstruction:
This page continues p.45. There Grothendieck rebuilt a three-stratum space U ⊂ V ⊂ W, equisingular along strata, from 'non-singular' data: manifolds with boundary, locally trivial fibrations and gluings. Here he (i) puts the 3-step construction into an inductive diagram, (ii) states the general n-step pattern and (iii) draws low-dimensional pictures.

(i) Top left. A filtration U_0 ⊂ U_1 ⊂ U_2 (⊂ U_3) of a stratified space. Each closed piece U_k is replaced by a compact 'core' U_k^0: a manifold with boundary (later with corners), i.e. the stratum minus an open tubular neighbourhood of the lower strata, so U_k^0 ↪ U_k.
- Level 1: ∂U_1^0 = U_0', the link bundle of U_0 in U_1, fibred over U_0.
- Level 2: ∂U_2^0 splits into two pieces glued along a common boundary. U_1^{0'} is fibred over U_1^0 with link fibres. U_0'' is fibred over U_0 with fibres that are manifolds with boundary (the truncated link of U_0 in U_2). They are glued along ∂U_1^{0'} = ∂U_0''.
- The curved arrows record that every boundary piece maps down to a lower core: U_1^{0'} → U_1^0 and U_0'' → U_0. They also record that the restriction of U_1^{0'} over ∂U_1^0 = U_0' is compatible with the fibration over U_0.
- Level 3 starts in the same way: ∂U_3^0 ⊃ U_2^{0'} → U_2^0, with ∂U_2^{0'} ⊂ U_2^{0'}.
- The original space is recovered by iterated pushouts. These are U_1 = U_1^0 ⊔_{U_0'} U_0, then U_2 = U_2^0 ⊔_{∂U_2^0} U_1, and so on.

(ii) Top right: the general pattern. U_n is reached from U_n^0, a manifold with corners. Its boundary ∂U_n^0 is a union of faces ∂_{n-1}U_n^0, ∂_{n-2}U_n^0, …, ∂_0U_n^0. Each face ∂_iU_n^0 is a locally trivial fibration over the core U_i^0 (with U_0^0 = U_0), and U_n is obtained by collapsing these fibrations.
- This is precisely the modern description of a Thom–Mather stratified space by a system of manifolds with corners carrying an 'iterated fibration structure': the faces are indexed by lower strata and fibre over the resolved lower strata.

(iii) Pictures.
- Dumbbell pictures: a 1-dimensional stratum (segment) with two 0-dimensional strata (endpoints) inside a 2-dimensional piece. The discs U'' around the endpoints are glued to the tube V^{0'} around the truncated segment V^0, along boundary pieces u, u'. This illustrates step 6 of p.45: V' = V^{0'} ⊔_∂ U''.
- Triangle/V figure and the wedge with regions I, II, III: a planar stratification near a point where several 1-strata meet. Region I is tube neighbourhoods of the 1-strata, region II the transition (corner) zones, region III the disc around the point.
- List 1°)–6°): a step-by-step build-up of the neighbourhood of a 0-stratum u in a 2-dimensional stratified germ.
  - 1°) The point U_0.
  - 2°) Its link points U_0'.
  - 3°) Rays U_1^0 emanating from it.
  - 4°) Thickened tubes U_1^{0'} around the rays.
  - 5°) The disc around the point glued to these tubes.
  - 6°) The 2-dimensional core U_2^0 filling the sectors, with corners where U_1^{0'} meets the disc.

The purpose is the 'dévissage' of tame (moderate) stratified spaces into non-singular data. Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 later conjectures this to be an equivalence of categories.
errors: The general diagram omits the compatibility conditions at corners. On ∂_iU_n^0 ∩ ∂_jU_n^0 (i<j) the fibration over U_j^0 must restrict over the face ∂_iU_j^0 compatibly with the fibration over U_i^0. This is the 'iterated fibration / control' condition, without which the gluing is not well defined. It is implicit in the level-2 identification ∂U_1^{0'} = ∂U_0'' but not stated in general.
In the general diagram ∂U_n^0 is written as if it were a disjoint union of the faces ∂_iU_n^0; in fact the faces are glued along corners, as the level-2 case shows.
On p.45, step 6 reads '∂U = ∂V^0' where ∂U'' = ∂V^{0'} is meant. This page uses the correct form ∂U_1^{0'} = ∂U''.

ideas.what: Reconstruction of an equisingular stratified space from cores that are manifolds with corners. Boundary faces are indexed by lower strata, each fibring over the core of that stratum, and the space is recovered by iterated collapse/gluing.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution / 'unfolding' / 'unzipping' of a Thom–Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners with iterated fibration structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) control data; Verona (1984) resolutions; Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012), Melrose; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) unzipping
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, as a conjectural 'théorème de dévissage' of tame stratified structures into non-singular ones (stated without these explicit diagrams)

ideas.what: Explicit two- and three-step instance: link bundle U_0', truncated link bundle U_0'' with fibres that are manifolds with boundary, glued to the tube U_1^{0'} along ∂.
ideas.modern_name: Tubular neighbourhood / link bundle gluing (plumbing of control data)

ideas.what: Planar pictures of the neighbourhood of a point stratum built in stages (point, link, rays, tubes, disc, sector cores).
ideas.modern_name: Conical structure / local triviality of stratified germs

missed.claim: This is a 1974 dated working form of the 'dévissage' later announced in Esquisse (1984). It already has the explicit inductive data: cores U_n^0, faces ∂_iU_n^0 fibred over U_i^0, and the gluings. This predates Verona's resolutions and the Melrose school's iterated fibration structures. It is a priority/historical detail rather than new mathematics.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the corner-resolution picture of stratified spaces as the intended 'non-singular model' of tame topology. This is relevant to the attribution of the equivalence between conically smooth stratified spaces and manifolds with corners carrying fibration data (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka).

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard (now well documented) resolution of Thom–Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with corners with iterated fibrations, and Grothendieck himself announced the dévissage in Esquisse. Only the early date and explicit diagram are of mild historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Top diagram: the arrows show U_1^0 ↪ U_1 and U_2^0 ↪ U_2. U_0'' carries a double prime and is fibred toward U_0; U_1^{0'} points to U_1^0.
Right diagram: the arrows go U_n → U_n^0 ⊃ ∂U_n^0, and from each face ∂_iU_n^0 down to U_i^0. They read 'U_{n-1}^0, U_{n-2}^0, …, U_0^0 = U_0'.
Dumbbell figure labels: U'' (both discs), V^{0'} (top and bottom of tube), V^0 (middle), and u, u' at each junction.
In 4°)–6°) the labels are mostly U_1^0 and U_1^{0'} (tube cores and their thickenings), plus U_2^0 in 6°); the point is labelled u / U_0.
